- Established exposure to global sourcing networks through international procurement and sales in the hardware trading segment
- Diversified object clause after FY2025-26 amendment, giving the Company optionality to build multiple revenue streams
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-segment concentration on computer hardware trading — The hardware trading segment was the sole meaningful operational driver in FY2025-26 while all four newly added verticals remained nascent, so the Company's earnings depend on one competitive, low-inventory trading activity.
- Component price volatility and rapid technological obsolescence — MD&A states the business is highly sensitive to price volatility in hardware components and to rapid technological obsolescence, which can strand inventory value and compress margins.
- Foreign exchange and cross-border regulatory exposure — A portion of trading involves cross-border procurement and sales, exposing the Company to FX fluctuations, import/export regulatory compliance and geopolitical uncertainty affecting global trade flows.
- FEMA non-compliance flagged by the auditor — The auditor observed that certain export proceeds were not realised within the prescribed six months and certain import payments were not settled within six months of shipment; the Directors attribute these to vendors not having been paid by their contracting parties and to technical issues at the Company's authorised bank — a live regulatory and receivable-recovery exposure.
- Credit exposure and counterparty reliability — MD&A flags credit exposure, counterparty reliability and inventory management as trading risks that may impact margins and cash-flow stability; the unrealised export proceeds are a concrete instance.
- Execution risk in the four newly added verticals — Infrastructure and construction, integrated technology solutions, strategic resource management, and logistics and air cargo are all at an early stage of operational development, each carrying project execution delays, technological disruption, operational inefficiency and dependence on external market conditions.
- Intense competition pressuring pricing and profitability — MD&A states the highly competitive nature of the industry exerts pressure on pricing and profitability, requiring continuous efficiency improvements and strong vendor relationships; management attributes the year's lower profitability to business transition and margin pressure.
- Compliance and internal-control maturity — The Directors' Report records that no UPSI structured digital database entry was maintained until June 2025 (complied only from October 2025) and that stock-exchange annual listing fees for FY2025-26 were not paid within time, indicating compliance-process gaps alongside an acknowledged need to strengthen internal controls and risk monitoring.

open.item: Management is focused on improving trading margins and establishing long-term supply chain relationships to ensure business stability and growth.

The four newly added verticals — infrastructure and construction, integrated technology solutions, strategic resource services, and logistics and air cargo — are expected to gradually scale up as market opportunities are identified and execution capabilities strengthened.

The auditor flagged FEMA non-compliance — unrealised export proceeds beyond six months and unsettled import payments beyond six months from shipment — which the Directors attribute to vendors' non-receipt of payments and technical issues at the Company's banker.
Management is working towards strengthening internal controls, improving risk monitoring systems and ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory frameworks.

The Company will further strengthen its vendor base, expand its customer network and enhance operational efficiency across domestic and international markets so hardware trading provides sustained revenue support.
The Company aims to leverage its diversified structure to build multiple revenue streams over time, scaling the four new verticals as opportunities are identified.

The Company added four new business objects — Infrastructure & Construction, Integrated Technologies Solutions, Strategic Resource Solutions and Logistics & Air Cargo — as the vehicle for expansion, with no capex quantum or project timeline disclosed.
